item.title: [PBV7-485] Bootstrap the standalone .NET 10 realtime solution
item.description:
Source and parent

Specification: Realtime WebSocket Platform – .NET 10, Redis, and Kubernetes
Parent Epic: PBV7-484

Context

Create the independently deployable solution and repository foundation from a blank starting point. The service must build, test, Native AOT-publish, containerize, and release without depending on the PBV7 application process or deployment.

Requirements

  • Create Propago.Realtime.sln and projects for Gateway, Contracts, Redis infrastructure, unit tests, integration tests, Kubernetes tests, and load tests.
  • Establish repository folders for source, tests, Helm, cluster configuration, observability, scripts, and documentation.
  • Target .NET 10 and use ASP.NET Core APIs compatible with Native AOT.
  • Configure source-generated System.Text.Json metadata for all protocol DTOs.
  • Add startup, readiness, and liveness endpoints with distinct semantics.
  • Add configuration validation, structured logging, metrics foundations, and graceful-host shutdown hooks.
  • Configure .NET SDK OCI container publishing with a non-root runtime and read-only filesystem where practical.
  • Establish independent semantic versioning for application, container, chart, and contracts.
  • Add CI checks for restore, build, unit tests, Native AOT publish, container creation, dependency review, image scanning, and SBOM generation.
  • Add a PowerShell 7 bootstrap/prerequisite script governed by Propago Scripts standard 4.0.
  • Document prerequisites, supported platforms, repository layout, local development, and build/publish instructions.

Dependencies

  • Access to the intended source repository and container registry.
  • Current .NET 10 SDK and approved CI runner images.
  • Current Propago Standards repository manifests.

Completion criteria

  • A clean checkout can restore, build, test, Native AOT-publish, and produce the OCI image without manual project creation.
  • There are no unresolved compiler, AOT, trimming, or source-generation warnings approved as blockers.
  • Gateway starts independently and exposes working startup, readiness, and liveness endpoints.
  • The runtime container executes as non-root and does not require the PBV7 application deployment.
  • Bootstrap automation is idempotent, documented, logged, and compliant with Scripts standard 4.0.
  • Architecture and developer onboarding documentation completes technical review.

Testing criteria

  • Run full unit tests from a clean checkout.
  • Perform full-file PowerShell parser validation for every generated or modified PowerShell file.
  • Validate explicit PowerShell 7, .NET SDK, Git, container CLI, path, permission, and registry prerequisites.
  • Execute the bootstrap twice and verify the second run reports existing resources as unchanged or skipped.
  • Start the Native AOT executable and validate all health endpoints.
  • Run the generated container rootless with its intended security settings.
  • Verify CI produces versioned, immutable artifacts, scan results, and SBOM output.
  • Verify failure paths produce non-zero exit codes, useful logs, and no credential disclosure.
